top10.introHtml: Refreshed 2026-09-23. Showing top 4-seat convertibles within 35 mi of Media, PA, $7k–$15k. Sources: Cars.com (10 listings post-filter / 26 found), CarGurus (21 listings post-filter / 76 found), AutoTrader (19 listings post-filter / 55 found). Excluded models: all 2-seat roadsters (Miata, Z3/Z4, Boxster, SLK, Z3, TT, Crossfire, Corvette, S2000, Solstice, Sky, 350Z/370Z, Smart Cabrio, Fiat 124), plus personal exclusions (MINI, Buick, Volvo, Toyota Solara, Camaro, pre-2005 Mustangs).

picks.whyGood: The G37 Convertible is one of the sharpest-looking soft-tops in budget. VQ37VHR V6 makes 325 hp, 7-speed auto is smooth, and the rear 2+2 seats are genuinely usable for adults on short trips. Faulkner Infiniti is a franchise dealer — clean title + no accidents on Cars.com, 91k miles on a VQ engine that routinely goes 200k with oil changes. Factory hard-top mechanism is robust. Media PA flagship dealer means you can actually get service.
picks.whatToVerify: Full power-top cycle (open and close twice); check headliner for water stains at A-pillars; rear window defroster function; rocker panel rust (common after 10+ winters); VQ timing chain tensioners (rattle on cold start = attention needed); differential fluid age.
picks.bottomLine: The best all-around pick — sporty V6 power, franchise-dealer provenance, and a convertible top that actually folds into a proper trunk lid.

picks.whyGood: S550-generation Mustang (2015–2023) is the modern benchmark. The EcoBoost 2.3T makes 310 hp, better real-world mpg than the GT, and the Tremec/SelectShift 10-speed auto is slick. CarGurus rates it 'Great Price' at $10,995 — that's a lot of convertible for the money. Fred Beans is a volume Ford dealer in Langhorne, likely off a trade-in with full service history. 132k miles is high but the 2.3T EcoBoost is a known truck/Bronco engine built for longevity.
picks.whatToVerify: Power-top full cycle; rear-seat water staining (common if top seal leaks); check for rear-camera function and SYNC updates; oil consumption test at idle; transmission fluid color; any deferred TSB for EcoBoost carbon buildup.
picks.bottomLine: Most car per dollar — modern safety tech, 310 hp, and a 'Great Price' flag from CarGurus make this the smart buy if mileage doesn't scare you.

picks.whyGood: 39,772 miles on a 2012 128i is extraordinary — this car barely moved. The naturally-aspirated N52 six is the simplest, most bulletproof BMW engine of the era (no turbos, no twin-scroll complexity). Clean title, no accidents on Cars.com. Selden Motors in Willow Grove has been selling BMWs forever. The 128i soft-top folds in under 20 seconds and has rear seats adults can actually sit in for short hops.
picks.whatToVerify: Top operation (full open/close, check hydraulic fluid level in trunk); rear-window plastic condition; coolant overflow bottle cracks (N52 issue); VANOS rattle on cold start; cooling system hose age; oil leaks at valve cover gasket.
picks.bottomLine: Ultra-low miles on a dead-reliable BMW six makes this the safest mechanical bet in the entire list.

picks.whyGood: S197 Mustang V6 (305 hp, 3.7 Duratec) is the sweet spot for a cheap fun convertible — reliable, cheap parts everywhere, and 30+ mpg highway. AutoTrader rates it 'Great Deal' at $8,952. 121k miles is fine for the 3.7. Josie's is a known Philly-area indie dealer.
picks.whatToVerify: Top seal condition (rear corners peel on S197s); 8.8 rear axle clunk on takeoff; spring perch rust (check under rear subframe); rear seat water staining; cam phaser rattle on cold start (less common on 3.7 vs 4.6); transmission fluid.
picks.bottomLine: The dollar-per-smile champion — $9k for a running, driving modern Mustang convertible is hard to beat.

picks.whyGood: 2009 CLK350 is literally 2 miles from Media PA — the closest listing in the search. The W209 CLK is one of the best-looking convertibles Mercedes ever made. 65k miles on a naturally-aspirated M272 V6 is genuinely low. Prime Autohaus in Media is local and easily re-visited for pre-purchase inspection. The fabric top is hydraulic and generally reliable if serviced.
picks.whatToVerify: Full top cycle and retraction check; hydraulic top fluid level (reservoir under trunk floor); M272 balance shaft wear (notorious on 2005-2007, less on 2008-2009 updated engines — verify build date); rear window defroster; AC compressor function.
picks.bottomLine: Local dealer, low miles, gorgeous W209 styling — if the balance shaft checks out, this is a neighborhood gem.

picks.whyGood: 435i xDrive (306 hp twin-scroll turbo) is serious fun, and at $8,500 with AutoTrader 'Great Deal' rating it's priced like a base Beetle. The F33 4-series hardtop convertible folds flush — no fabric top concerns. xDrive AWD gives year-round usability. 140k miles is the main asterisk; the N55 turbo is robust if maintained.
picks.whatToVerify: Oil catch can / separator condition (N55 oil consumption); cooling system (expansion tank cracks); soft-top or retractable hardtop: verify full cycle and check hydraulic lines; check for timing chain tensioner updates; inspect trunk drain tubes; differential fluid.
picks.bottomLine: 306 hp xDrive BMW hardtop at $8,500 is an outlier deal — the miles are real but the N55 handles them well.

picks.whyGood: 57k miles on an E46/E90 3-series is rare and this trim says 'Ci' which is the clean BMW nomenclature for the coupe-convertible. N52 or M54 engine at these miles is essentially new. Clean title and no accidents on Cars.com. The E90-gen 3 series has rear seats passengers can actually use.
picks.whatToVerify: Verify it's the E46 generation (2006 is actually E90 era — confirm 'Ci' designation which was E46 through 2006); full top cycle; cooling system (E46 expansion tanks crack); subframe bushing condition; oil leaks at VANOS, valve cover.
picks.bottomLine: Low-mile BMW convertible at under $13k — if the top works and the cooling system checks out, this is a keeper.

picks.whyGood: The A5 Cabriolet is the best-looking convertible in any price range. 2.0T quattro means AWD grip in the rain and respectable 211 hp. 91k miles on the 2.0T is mid-life. The fabric top is fabric but well-engineered — usually good to 150k with care.
picks.whatToVerify: Top operation (fabric tears at rear corners); drain tube function (Audi cabrios flood cabin if drains clog); timing chain (2.0 TFSI can rattle on cold start = tensioner issue); DSG or CVT fluid service history; Haldex AWD service.
picks.bottomLine: Drop-dead gorgeous convertible with AWD grip — just budget for top drain maintenance and timing chain inspection.

picks.whyGood: Cheapest BMW convertible on any site at $7,485. SULEV designation = California emissions-grade engine, which often indicates better maintenance history. N52 six is indestructible at 147k. Clean title, no accidents. Good budget pick if you want rear seats and a proper BMW experience.
picks.whatToVerify: Top hydraulic operation; rear window delamination or yellowing; cooling system (expansion tank, water pump); VANOS; rocker panel rust; service history for 147k miles.
picks.bottomLine: The most accessible BMW convertible here — great value if you're comfortable with the mileage and can verify service history.

picks.whyGood: Second CLK350 on the list but this one has only 49k miles — a near-new W209. The later 2009 build avoids the balance shaft issue that plagued 2005-2007 units. The W209 CLK is a genuinely pretty car with a proper 4-seat fabric top. Josie's is a trusted area indie.
picks.whatToVerify: Balance shaft confirmation (2009 should be fine but verify VIN build date); full top hydraulic cycle; M272 coolant passages; AC compressor; interior water staining check.
picks.bottomLine: Near-museum-quality miles on a beautiful CLK — worth $13,500 if the inspection comes back clean.

manual10.introHtml: No manual-transmission 4-seat convertibles surfaced in this refresh within 35 miles of Media, PA between $7k–$15k. Manual convertibles in this price band are genuinely scarce — most 4-seat soft-tops (BMW, Mercedes, Infiniti, Mustang) came predominantly with automatics. If a manual Mustang GT or BMW 3-series pops up at Josie's or Car Cheer, it won't last long. Consider expanding the radius to 50 miles or removing the no-accidents filter for a second-run manual-specific search.

mustangs.introHtml: 2005+ Ford Mustang convertibles only (S197 and S550 generations). 3 units found in budget within 35 mi. Note: only 1 unique car found (a 2020 EcoBoost Premium at Langhorne and a 2014 V6) — the rank 3 pick is the same 2020 car listed on AutoTrader vs. CarGurus.

picks.whyGood: S550 gen (2015–2023) with EcoBoost Premium = modern Mustang at a steal. CarGurus 'Great Price' badge. Fred Beans is a high-volume Philly-area Ford dealer with service history likely on file. EcoBoost 2.3T is the same engine as the Focus RS and Explorer ST — proven long-term. Premium trim = heated seats, SYNC 3, Brembo brake option.
picks.whatToVerify: Carbon buildup on EcoBoost intake (walnut blasting if needed); power-top full cycle + rear window defroster; rear seat water staining from top seal; rear camera function; oil consumption at idle; check TSB status.
picks.bottomLine: Best value modern Mustang convertible in budget — S550 refinement and reliability at a fraction of new price.

picks.whyGood: Final-year S197 Mustang at a 'Great Deal' price. The 3.7 Duratec V6 makes 305 hp and 30 mpg highway — no apologies needed. 121k on a Duratec is barely broken in. Josie's is a well-known Gilbertsville dealer with a real inventory.
picks.whatToVerify: S197-specific: check top latch pins (wear allows wind noise); spring perch rust under rear subframe; rear differential clunk on takeoff; cam phaser rattle on cold start (3.7 is less prone than 4.6 but check); transmission fluid.
picks.bottomLine: Final S197 at under $9k — fun, practical, and cheap to maintain anywhere in the country.

picks.whyGood: Same 2020 EcoBoost Premium listed on AutoTrader — useful for cross-checking dealer pricing and getting a second CarFax pull. Fred Beans Ford's listing on AutoTrader may show different photos or condition notes than the CarGurus listing.
picks.whatToVerify: Same checks as rank 1: top cycle, carbon, water staining, TSBs. Compare CarFax history from both site pulls.
picks.bottomLine: Same great car — listed on a second platform, giving you negotiating leverage and history comparison.
